newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish TSB concerned by lack of progress on merger.
newsitem.headline: Irish TSB concerned by lack of progress on merger.

text.p: Ireland's TSB Bank Plc said on Friday that it was regrettable that no progress had been reported on the proposed merger of the bank with a strategic partner.

"The protracted delay in finalising a disposal decision on the bank is of concern to us, notwithstanding the satisfactory performance of the bank in the years since the merger strategy was first proposed," TSB said in its annual results statement.
In April, 1994, TSB's trustees recommended that the bank be sold to National Australia Bank Ltd and merged with NAB's Irish arm, National Irish Bank (NIB).
A number of other institutions, including Ulster Bank, a unit of National Westminster Bank Plc, are also interested in acquiring TSB.
Any sale of TSB has to be approved by the government, to whom the proceeds of the deal accrue, but such approval has not yet been given.
The bank said the delay in agreeing the merger was not frustrating its business plans, however.

"The climate of uncertainty is an incentive rather than a deterrent for the trustees to take all the necessary operational and investment initiatives to secure the enhancement of the bank's assets and the security of our employees," chairman Dermot Whelan said.
The bank said it had continued with its own investment programme in human resources, new and refurbished bank branches, technology products and services.

By the end of March, TSB customers will have access to more than 800 ATMs including those of Allied Irish Banks, Bank of Ireland and Ulster Bank which should lead to further growth in current accounts, TSB said.
The bank is also looking at telesales access for customers but said it would be 1998 before a telebanking services was up and running.
It also said preparation for the advent of the euro was well advanced.
